study_identification_part.si4_title: Lifespan Normative Modeling of Brain Microstructure

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the aim to present the first large-scale normative model of white matter microstructure across the lifespan and to demonstrate its clinical utility (diagnostic/individual-level deviation detection) in MCI, Alzheimer's disease, and 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, satisfying both hypothesis/purpose and normative modeling purpose criteria.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Here we present the first large-scale normative model of brain WM microstructure based on 19 international diffusion MRI datasets covering almost the entire lifespan... We illustrate the utility of the method by applying it to detect and visualize profiles of WM microstructural deviations in ... mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, and 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: For building a new model, the study uses controls from multiple datasets and details image quality procedures: manual QC for several datasets and algorithmic outlier removal (isolation forests) for others; it reports the final training N and mentions that counts reflect post-QC exclusions. It also clarifies that only control subjects from clinical datasets were used to define the reference model.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: All study participants had ... a usable dMRI scan. ADNI3, OASIS3, PPMI, CAMCAN and HBN were manually checked for head movement, FOV related artifacts and other dMRI acquisition artifacts and preprocessing errors... For all other datasets used for training, outliers were detected with an anomaly detection algorithm called isolation forests... a total of 54,583 subjects remained for training. For clinical samples (HBN, ADNI3, OASIS3 and PPMI), only the control subjects are shown (as they were the only ones used to define the normative model). Footnote: The N for each group reflects the participants after quality control and removal of outliers.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: Section 3. Quality control; Figure 1 caption; Footnote near line ~105

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly modeled (age via cubic B-splines; sex as grouping). Multi-site/batch effects are addressed by modeling dMRI protocol as batch in HBR with partial pooling; harmonization occurs at the Z-score level, aligning with accepted site-effect handling.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: We added age and sex as the covariates for the present study and we modeled the non-linear effect of age with a cubic b-spline basis set... we used the dMRI protocol as the batch effect when training the normative model with HBR... Normative modeling with HBR adjusts the Z-scores instead of the input data points.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The study specifies that it pools data from 19 international/public studies, names common datasets in text/captions/references, and the supplement enumerates 37 acquisition protocols across those studies (Table S1), satisfying data source specification.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: ...based on 19 international diffusion MRI datasets covering almost the entire lifespan... We identified 37 dMRI acquisition protocols across the 19 datasets (see Table S1).
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.location: VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: Abstract; Section 6; media-1.pdf.md: Table S1 caption

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Per guidance, for secondary data (existing datasets), this item is not applicable. This study builds a new model using existing public datasets rather than primary data collection.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: ...based on 19 international diffusion MRI datasets... We identified 37 dMRI acquisition protocols across the 19 datasets (secondary data; summarized in Supplementary Table S1).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing tools and steps are specified per dataset in the supplement (e.g., DiPy LPCA/MPPCA denoising, MRTRIX, TOPUP/Synb0, FSL-EDDY, registration), and QC procedures are described in the main text (manual checks and isolation forest outlier removal).
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: ADNI3: DiPy LPCA/MPPCA; MRTRIX; T1 warp; FSL-EDDY; FSL. OASIS3: DiPy MPPCA; MRTRIX; TOPUP-SynB0; FSL-EDDY; FSL. NIMHANS: DiPy LPCA; DiPy; TOPUP-SynB0; FSL-EDDY; DiPy. UCLA: DiPy LPCA; DiPy; TOPUP; FSL-EDDY; DiPy. (See preprocessing table). Also: 'ADNI3, OASIS3, PPMI, CAMCAN and HBN were manually checked... For all other datasets ... isolation forests ... outlier subjects... removed.'
nm5_data_preprocessing.location: media-1.pdf.md: Preprocessing table (~lines 500–520); VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: Section 3. Quality control

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The model uses repeated train/test data splits (10 iterations) and reports diagnostics on held-out tests, satisfying internal validation with partitioning.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The trajectories represent the average of the simulated data across the 10 different train_test data splits... We ran these fit validation metrics ... for each ROI across all 10 experimental iterations.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.location: media-1.pdf.md: Figure S1–S4 captions; VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: model validation text (~line 271)

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The trained reference model is adapted to two new independent datasets; 50% of healthy controls are used for recalibration, and the remaining 50% healthy controls plus patients are used for anomaly detection, demonstrating application to independent healthy data not used for model development.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: We adapted the large-scale trained reference model to healthy controls from two new independent datasets... For each dataset we used 50% of the healthy controls for recalibrating the model. Thereafter, the remaining 50% of healthy controls and the patients were used for anomaly detection...

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The approach is Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR) with age modeled via cubic B-splines and batch effects for protocol and sex; implementation via PCNtoolkit (v29) in Python 3.9, with explicit description of harmonization at the Z-score level and HBR options in the supplement.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: The HBR NM framework is ... we modeled the non-linear effect of age with a cubic b-spline... we used the dMRI protocol as the batch effect... We ran the training and testing ... using the PCNtoolkit package (v29) and Python 3.9... Normative modeling with HBR adjusts the Z-scores instead of the input data points... In this paper we used the following options for the HBR algorithm...
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.location: VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: Sections 5–6; media-1.pdf.md: 'HBR specific parameters' section (~lines 520–540)

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: To test model accuracy, we ran two diagnostic metrics... standardized mean squared error (SMSE)... mean standardized log loss (MSLL)... Additionally... we calculated Shapiro-Wilk's W, the kurtosis and the skewness of the estimated Z-scores...
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.location: VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: Results text (~lines 120–140) and model validation (~line 271); media-1.pdf.md: Figures S5–S8
